mission: LÉLU 2.1 — geometry fidelity and mathematical validation
observed: Projection cost was measured structurally for 4 variants: 15 draw calls each, GPU bytes 27.6/26.3/21.5/18.5 MB, parse 105.7/56.8/77.7/72.7 ms. No frame time was measured on any device.
studied: What a static projection measurement can and cannot say about real-time performance.
question: Does the tube hair hold a mobile frame budget?
hypothesis: Lower triangle counts imply a proportionally lower frame time.
method: Parse each GLB, count triangles and draw calls, estimate GPU bytes, and time the parse. Do not extrapolate to frames.
results: Triangle and memory cost fall with LOD; frame time is unmeasured. The honest statement is structural: the binding cost is not known.

evidence.note: draw calls, triangles, GPU bytes, parse time, no frame time
asserts the 'no frame time' note is still there

learned: Triangle count is a proxy for GPU work only when the bottleneck is vertex processing. Nothing in this data establishes that, so no iPhone or real-time claim can be made.
limitations: No device or browser benchmark was run; p50/p95 frame times and LOD transition cost are unknown.
GPU byte estimates are derived from buffer sizes, not from measured upload.
applications: The LOD ladder is ready for a device benchmark that has not happened yet.
nextQuestions: What is p50/p95 frame time for tubes-high on a mid-range phone at 1080p?
At what screen coverage does the high LOD stop being affordable?
